record.paper_title: Open questions in quarkonium and electromagnetic probes
record.context_brief: J/psi baseline and energy-dependent nuclear absorption
record.original_question: For J/ψ production at SPS and RHIC energies, how does the effective nuclear absorption cross section σ_abs depend on collision energy once one consistently includes initial-state nuclear modifications of the parton distribution functions, final-state absorption, and feed-down from higher charmonium states such as ψ′ and χ_c, and what baseline should therefore be used when judging whether the J/ψ suppression observed in heavy-ion collisions is genuinely anomalous?

evidence.quote: The observation that the σabs values at SPS and RHIC energies are considerably different raises the question of whether σabs varies within the energy range covered by the fixed-target experiments.
At this moment, however, in the absence of that measurement, we cannot really argue that we have a robust reference baseline at the energy of the heavy-ion data.

Hence, the "anomalous" aspect of the J/ψ suppression pattern seen in heavy-ion collisions has not yet been convincingly demonstrated, and requires, in particular, a more detailed understanding of charmonia production in elementary pp and p-A collisions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider J/ψ production in proton–proton, proton–nucleus, and nucleus–nucleus collisions at center-of-mass energies ranging from fixed-target SPS energies (√s_NN ≈ 17–29 GeV) up to RHIC energies (√s_NN = 200 GeV). The inclusive J/ψ yield in these reactions receives contributions from direct production and from feed-down decays of higher charmonium states, in particular ψ′ → J/ψ + X and χ_c → J/ψ + γ. In a Glauber-type model the J/ψ yield in p–A and A–A collisions, relative to the binary-scaled pp yield, is modified by (i) initial-state nuclear modifications of the parton distribution functions (nuclear shadowing/antishadowing), (ii) effective final-state absorption of the pre-resonant or formed charmonium state on cold nuclear matter, parametrized by an effective absorption cross section σ_abs, and (iii) the differing absorption cross sections of the feed-down components.

(a) Determine, within a self-consistent treatment that incorporates all three effects above, the dependence of the effective σ_abs(√s_NN) on the collision energy across the SPS-to-RHIC range.

(b) Using this energy-dependent σ_abs together with the appropriate nuclear PDFs and feed-down decomposition, construct the "cold nuclear matter" baseline for the J/ψ nuclear modification factor R_AA in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies, and quantify whether, and at what level of significance, the J/ψ suppression observed in heavy-ion collisions exceeds this baseline (i.e. is genuinely "anomalous").
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent analyses (e.g., Lourenço–Vogt–Wöhri, JHEP 2009; Phys. Rev. C 76, 064906) have parametrized a decreasing effective σ_abs with increasing √s_NN using p–A data from 200 to 920 GeV beam energies and RHIC d-Au data at 200 GeV, providing improved cold-nuclear-matter baselines. Nevertheless, residual uncertainties from nuclear PDFs, the production mechanism, and the feed-down decomposition remain, so a fully consensus baseline establishing or refuting "anomalous" J/ψ suppression at SPS and RHIC energies has not been definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: Energy dependence of J/ψ absorption in proton-nucleus collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes J/ψ production cross sections in p-A from 200 to 920 GeV and in d-Au at √s=200 GeV using Glauber formalism, extracting an energy-dependent effective σ_abs.
status_evidence.claim: Provides explicit parametrization of σ_abs(√s) consistent across SPS and RHIC fixed-target/p-A data.

status_evidence.title: J/ψ suppression and the decrease of nuclear absorption with increasing energy
status_evidence.snippet: Shows σ_abs decreases with increasing collision energy, modifying the cold-nuclear-matter baseline for heavy-ion data.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates an energy-dependent decrease of σ_abs, refining the baseline used to assess anomalous suppression.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear absorption and anomalous J/psi suppression in Pb+Pb collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses interplay between nuclear absorption and the anomalous suppression component in Pb+Pb at SPS.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that the anomalous component depends sensitively on the assumed σ_abs and feed-down treatment.
